title: The Galois action on étale cohomology of geometric fibres
summary: Constructs the action ρ(σ) = c_σ ∘ σ_X^* of the absolute Galois group on étale and pro-étale cohomology of geometric fibres of rigid spaces over any complete non-archimedean field and of schemes over any field, with the identification G_K ≅ Aut_cont(C/K), functoriality, discreteness, the dictionary with higher direct images to the base point, the Hochschild–Serre E_2 term, agreement with the scheme adic action and Frobenius conventions, ℓ-adic and rational coefficients as continuous representations, equivariant twisting, equivariant comparison for proper schemes, and the passage from finiteness to finitely generated and finite-dimensional representations.

layers.title: The Galois group and the completed algebraic closure

targets.name: completedAlgClosure
targets.statement: For K complete for a nontrivial non-archimedean rank-one absolute value (any characteristic), K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K with the spectral norm and C = UniformSpace.Completion K̄: K^sep = SeparableClosure K is dense in C; C is algebraically closed; (C, 𝒪_C) is a geometric field pair and ξ_C : Spa(C,𝒪_C) → Spa(K,𝒪_K) is a geometric point; Spa(C,𝒪_C) ∼ lim_L Spa(L,𝒪_L) over finite subextensions L of K^sep/K is a colimit-presented tilde-limit.

api.name: sepClosure_dense
api.statement: K^sep is dense in K̄ and in C (separable approximations X^{p^e} − tX − b, continuity of roots)

api.name: isAlgClosed
api.statement: C is algebraically closed in every characteristic

api.name: geometricPoint
api.statement: ξ_C is an AdicSpace.GeometricPoint of Spa(K,𝒪_K)

api.name: tildeLimit
api.statement: Spa(C,𝒪_C) ∼ lim_L Spa(L,𝒪_L), colimit-presented, with finite-stage detection 𝒪_L ∩ ϖ^n𝒪_{K^sep} = ϖ^n𝒪_L

tests.name: padic
tests.statement: for K = ℚ_p, C is PadicComplex p up to the isometric ℚ_p-isomorphism AlgebraicClosure ℚ_p ≅ PadicAlgCl p

tests.name: charp
tests.statement: for K = 𝔽_p((t)), t^{1/p} ∉ K^sep is the limit of roots of X^p − sX − t as s → 0, and C is algebraically closed although IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange (CharZero) does not apply

tests.name: algclosed
tests.statement: if K is algebraically closed, K̄ = K = C and ξ_C = id

tests.name: not_complete
tests.statement: K̄ itself is not complete for K = ℚ_p; Spa(K̄) is not a geometric point in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry A1.7

tests.name: norm_unique
tests.statement: on ℚ_p(√p) the norm max(|a|,|b|) gives |√p| = 1 ≠ p^{-1/2} and is excluded by uniqueness of the power-multiplicative extension

targets.name: galoisCompletionEquiv
targets.statement: For σ ∈ G_K = Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K, σ̂ := UniformSpace.Completion.map σ is the unique continuous extension of σ to C, an isometric K-algebra automorphism preserving 𝒪_C and 𝔪_C; σ ↦ σ̂ is a group isomorphism G_K ≅ Aut_cont(C/K); the action map G_K × C → C is jointly continuous for the Krull topology; it is compatible with restriction to G_L for finite L ⊆ K̄ and with change of algebraic closure (τ̂ σ̂ τ̂⁻¹ = (τστ⁻¹)^).

api.name: surjective
api.statement: every continuous K-algebra endomorphism of C is some σ̂

api.name: continuous_action
api.statement: G_K × C → C jointly continuous

api.name: restrict
api.statement: for finite L ⊆ K̄ and σ ∈ G_L the extension over L equals the extension over K

api.name: conj
api.statement: change of algebraic closure conjugates σ̂

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: 1̂ = id_C

tests.name: sqrt3
tests.statement: for K = ℚ_3 and σ(√3) = −√3, σ̂ ≠ id

tests.name: padic_period_rings
tests.statement: for K/ℚ_p finite, σ̂ is PadicPeriodRings §1.1 completedGaloisAction after the isometry of 0.1

tests.name: discontinuous
tests.statement: discontinuous field automorphisms of ℂ_p are not in Aut_cont(ℂ_p/ℚ_p)

tests.name: charp_insep
tests.statement: for K = 𝔽_p((t)), σ̂ fixes t^{1/p}

targets.name: geometricPointAutEquiv
targets.statement: Every morphism a : Spa(C,𝒪_C) → Spa(C,𝒪_C) with ξ_C ∘ a = ξ_C is Spa(σ̂) for a unique σ ∈ G_K, and σ ↦ Spa(σ̂) is an anti-isomorphism of G_K onto these automorphisms. The connected pointed étale neighbourhoods (Spa(L,𝒪_L), v̄) of ξ_C, L/K finite separable, form a full subcategory of the cofiltered category N(ξ_C) of pointed étale neighbourhoods that is initial (every neighbourhood receives a morphism from one of them) and equivalent to the opposite P^op of the inclusion poset P of finite subextensions of K^sep/K: a morphism (Spa(L′,𝒪_{L′}), v̄′) → (Spa(L,𝒪_L), v̄) exists, and is unique, exactly when ι(L) ⊆ ι′(L′). Stalks are colimits over N(ξ_C)^op, hence F_{ξ_C} = colim_{L ∈ P} F(Spa(L,𝒪_L)), inclusion-filtered. An étale Spa(K,𝒪_K)-space is a disjoint union of such one-point spaces and v̄ factors through the component containing its image. On a connected neighbourhood, precomposition of v̄ with Spa(σ̂) is postcomposition of the embedding L → K^sep ⊆ C with σ. This fixes the Galois action on stalks: σ sends (V, v̄) to (V, v̄ ∘ Spa(σ̂)).

api.name: anti_mul
api.statement: Spa((στ)^) = Spa(τ̂) ∘ Spa(σ̂)

api.name: stalk_action_left
api.statement: the induced action on stalks is a left action

api.name: connected_initial
api.statement: connected neighbourhoods (Spa(L,𝒪_L), v̄) form an initial full subcategory of N(ξ_C), equivalent to P^op (arrows from the larger field to the smaller); a disconnected neighbourhood is refined to the component through v̄; F_{ξ_C} = colim_{N(ξ_C)^op} F(V) = colim_{L ∈ P} F(Spa(L,𝒪_L))

tests.name: quadratic
tests.statement: for a separable quadratic L/K (L = K(√a), a ∉ K^{×2}, char K ≠ 2; or the Artin–Schreier L = K(α), α² + α = t⁻¹, over K = 𝔽_2((t))), Hom_K(L,C) has two elements and the nontrivial class of G_K/G_L swaps them

tests.name: cubic
tests.statement: for L/K cyclic cubic, σ sends τ₀ to g∘τ₀; the opposite convention gives g⁻¹∘τ₀ and a right action

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: for K = C the only automorphism is the identity

tests.name: inseparable_quadratic
tests.statement: K = 𝔽_2((t)), L = K(t^{1/2}): [L:K] = 2 but Hom_K(L,C) has one element, G_L = G_K, and Spa(L,𝒪_L) → Spa(K,𝒪_K) is not étale, so it is not a neighbourhood

tests.name: disconnected
tests.statement: V = Spa(K,𝒪_K) ⊔ Spa(K,𝒪_K) pointed through the first component has two components and is not Spa of a field; it is refined by the first component, and a section (s_1, s_2) has the germ of s_1

tests.name: direction
tests.statement: K = ℚ_3, L = K(√3): N(ξ_C) has one morphism (Spa(L,𝒪_L), v̄) → (Spa(K,𝒪_K), ξ_C) and none back, whereas P has the arrow K → L only; N(ξ_C) has the terminal object (Spa(K,𝒪_K), ξ_C) and P has no largest element, so the neighbourhoods match P^op, not P; the stalk colimit runs over P with restriction F(Spa K) → F(Spa L)

targets.name: coverAutAction
targets.statement: In the settings (a) analytic étale sites of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, (b) pro-étale sites of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, (c) small étale sites of schemes: for p : Y → X, an automorphism a of Y with p ∘ a = p, a ring Λ and M ∈ D(X_τ, Λ), the unbounded derived category of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.1 (D⁺(X_τ, Λ) the bounded-below case), define c_a : a^{-1}p^{-1}M ≅ p^{-1}M from the pseudofunctor coherence and p ∘ a = p, and a^♮ := H^i(c_a) ∘ a^* on H^i(Y, p^{-1}M) and RΓ(Y, p^{-1}M), with a^* from the enhanced adjunction a^{-1} ⊣ Ra_* of EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.4 (on D⁺ the cohomology pullback of SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.1 and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §1.1).
hypotheses: Λ any ring; M ∈ D(X_τ, Λ), with D⁺(X_τ, Λ) as the bounded-below case
Λ commutative in the cup-product clause

api.name: comp
api.statement: (a∘b)^♮ = b^♮ ∘ a^♮ and id^♮ = id (cocycle identity for c)

api.name: degree_zero
api.statement: for ℱ = h_V with V étale over X, H⁰(Y,p^{-1}h_V) = Hom_X(Y,V) and a^♮(s) = s ∘ a

api.name: linear_natural
api.statement: Λ-linear, natural in M for morphisms in D(X_τ, Λ), compatible with change of coefficients

api.name: delta
api.statement: commutes with connecting maps of distinguished triangles in D(X_τ, Λ) (on D⁺, Sheaf.H.pullback_δ)

api.name: base_change
api.statement: for g : X′ → X, (a × id)^♮ ∘ g_Y^* = g_Y^* ∘ a^♮

api.name: cup
api.statement: for Λ commutative and M, N ∈ D(X_τ, Λ), a^♮(x ∪ y) = a^♮x ∪ a^♮y for the cup product into H^{i+j}(Y, p^{-1}(M ⊗^L_Λ N)) from EnhancedDerivedSheaves §§0.3–0.4 (EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.1 on schemes with finite coefficients); M ⊗^L_Λ N lies in D⁺ when M, N ∈ D⁺ and one factor has finite Tor amplitude, not in general; no cup product for noncommutative Λ

api.name: galois_cover
api.statement: for a finite étale Galois cover with group G, g ↦ (g⁻¹)^♮ is the G-module structure in the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §1.3(a) and SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15

tests.name: mu_n
tests.statement: X = Spa(K,𝒪_K), Y = Spa(C,𝒪_C), a = Spa(σ̂), ℱ = μ_n: a^♮(ζ) = σ(ζ); (a⁻¹)^♮ would give σ⁻¹(ζ)

tests.name: swap
tests.statement: X a point, Y = X ⊔ X, a the swap: a^♮ swaps the coordinates of ℤ²; a = id gives id

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: Y = ∅: all groups vanish

tests.name: order
tests.statement: on H⁰(Spa(L ⊗_K C), ℤ) = ℤ^{Gal(L/K)} for L/K Galois with group S₃ (K = ℚ_2, splitting field of T³ − 2), σ, τ ∈ G_K restricting to s of order 2 and r of order 3, a = Spa(id_L ⊗ σ̂), b = Spa(id_L ⊗ τ̂): (a∘b)^♮ = b^♮∘a^♮ sends δ_1 to δ_{rs}, the wrong order a^♮∘b^♮ sends it to δ_{sr} ≠ δ_{rs}; a cyclic extension (abelian group) does not separate the orders

tests.name: unbounded_tensor
tests.statement: X = Spa(K,𝒪_K), Y = Spa(C,𝒪_C), Λ = ℤ/4, M = N = ℤ/2: H^{−n}(Y, p^{-1}(M ⊗^L_Λ N)) = Tor_n^{ℤ/4}(ℤ/2, ℤ/2) = ℤ/2 for all n ≥ 0, a target outside D⁺, with trivial a^♮; M = Λ gives M ⊗^L N = N

tests.name: noncommutative
tests.statement: Λ = M_2(𝔽_2): the additive action exists, but a left module is not a right module by the same matrices (v = e_1, A = E_{12}, B = E_{21}: BAv = 0, ABv = e_1), so no cup product is formed

targets.name: rigidGaloisAction
targets.statement: For a rigid K-space X and σ ∈ G_K, σ_X := id_X × Spa(σ̂) : X_C → X_C satisfies pr_C ∘ σ_X = pr_C, (στ)_X = τ_X ∘ σ_X, 1_X = id, and for X ≠ ∅, σ ≠ 1 is not a morphism over Spa(C,𝒪_C). For M ∈ D(X_ét, Λ) (in particular M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ)), ρ(σ) := (σ_X)^♮ is a left action of G_K on H^i(X_C, M_C) and RΓ(X_C, M_C) by Λ-linear automorphisms; the same on pro-étale cohomology of pullbacks of objects of D⁺(X_proét, Λ), and for M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), H^i(X_C,ét, M_C) ≅ H^i(X_C,proét, ν^*M_C) is ρ-equivariant.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over Spa(K,𝒪_K)

api.name: over_X
api.statement: pr_C ∘ σ_X = pr_C; σ_X is an automorphism over X with inverse (σ⁻¹)_X

api.name: right_action
api.statement: (στ)_X = τ_X ∘ σ_X

api.name: not_over_C
api.statement: q ∘ σ_X = Spa(σ̂) ∘ q; not over Spa(C) if X ≠ ∅ and σ ≠ 1

api.name: left_action
api.statement: ρ(στ) = ρ(σ)ρ(τ), ρ(1) = id, Λ-linear

api.name: proetale
api.statement: pro-étale version and ν-compatibility

tests.name: point_mu_n
tests.statement: X = Spa(K,𝒪_K), ℱ = μ_n: ρ(σ)ζ = σ(ζ)

tests.name: permutation
tests.statement: X = Spa(L,𝒪_L): σ_X maps component τ to σ⁻¹∘τ and ρ(σ)δ_τ = δ_{σ∘τ}, the permutation representation ℤ[G_K/G_L] induced from the trivial representation of G_L; regular (of Gal(L/K), inflated) only for L/K Galois: for the non-Galois cubic ℚ_2(2^{1/3})/ℚ_2, rank 3 and transposition trace 1 versus rank 6 and trace 0; σ ↦ ρ(σ⁻¹) is not a homomorphism for an S₃-extension

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: K = C: ρ trivial; X = ∅: all groups vanish

tests.name: abelian_pullback
tests.statement: H⁰(Spa(C), pr^{-1}𝒪_{X_ét}) = K^sep for X = Spa(K,𝒪_K), not C (module pullback would give C)

targets.name: rigidGaloisAction_functorial
targets.statement: ρ commutes with (a) pullback along morphisms g : X′ → X of rigid K-spaces, (b) maps induced by morphisms in D(X_ét, Λ), (c) connecting maps of short exact sequences of sheaves of Λ-modules, (d) for Λ commutative, cup products into H^{i+j}(X_C, (M ⊗^L_Λ N)_C), with M ⊗^L_Λ N ∈ D(X_ét, Λ), in D⁺ when M, N are bounded below and one factor has finite Tor amplitude; (e) for finite L ⊆ K̄ (not necessarily separable), (X_L)_C = X_C and the G_L-action is the restriction of ρ; (f) for a K-isomorphism τ : K̄ → K̄′, id × Spa(τ̂⁻¹) intertwines ρ′(τστ⁻¹) with ρ(σ).
hypotheses: M, N ∈ D(X_ét, Λ) (in particular D⁺(X_ét, Λ))

tests.name: conj_self
tests.statement: in (f) with K̄′ = K̄ and τ ∈ G_K, id_X × Spa(τ̂⁻¹) = (τ⁻¹)_X induces ρ(τ⁻¹) = ρ(τ)⁻¹ and the statement is ρ(τ)⁻¹ρ(τστ⁻¹)ρ(τ) = ρ(σ); with ρ(τ) in its place it would read ρ(σ) = ρ(τ²στ⁻²), false for non-commuting σ, τ

tests.name: kummer
tests.statement: Kummer sequence on Spa(K): H⁰ gives 0 → μ_n(C) → (K^sep)^× → (K^sep)^× → 0 of discrete modules

tests.name: purely_inseparable
tests.statement: L = K(t^{1/p}) over 𝔽_p((t)): G_L = G_K and the actions agree

tests.name: tensor_target
tests.statement: (d) for X = Spa(K,𝒪_K), M = N = ℤ/2: over Λ = ℤ/2 the target is ℤ/2 in degree 0; over Λ = ℤ/4 it has H^{−n} = ℤ/2 for every n ≥ 0, outside D⁺, with trivial action

targets.name: schemeGaloisAction
targets.statement: For a scheme X over a field k and σ ∈ G_k, σ_X := id_X × Spec(σ|_{k^sep}) on X_{k^sep} and ρ(σ) := (σ_X)^♮ on H^i(X_{k^sep}, M) for M ∈ D(X_ét, Λ) (in particular D⁺): a left action by Λ-linear automorphisms with the functoriality of 1.3 (cup products for commutative Λ, EnhancedDerivedSheaves §0.3; EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.1 for finite coefficients); the pullback H^i(X_{k^sep}, M) → H^i(X_{k̄}, M) is an equivariant isomorphism; compatible with extensions k ⊆ k′.

api.name: left_action
api.statement: (στ)_X = τ_X ∘ σ_X, ρ left action

api.name: sep_vs_alg
api.statement: equivariant iso H^i(X_{k^sep},M) ≅ H^i(X_{k̄},M)

api.name: field_change
api.statement: equivariant for G_{k′} → G_k

tests.name: real
tests.statement: k = ℝ, n = 4: complex conjugation sends i to −i on H⁰(Spec ℂ, μ_4)

tests.name: frobenius
tests.statement: k = 𝔽_q: arithmetic Frobenius acts on μ_{ℓ^n}(k^sep) by ζ ↦ ζ^q

tests.name: permutation
tests.statement: X = Spec k′: ρ(σ)δ_τ = δ_{σ∘τ} on ℤ^{Hom_k(k′,k^sep)}

targets.name: rigidGaloisAction_colimit
targets.statement: For X a qcqs rigid K-space and M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) (any abelian sheaf, no torsion hypothesis), the pullbacks induce colim_L H^i(X_L, M_L) ≅ H^i(X_C, M_C) over finite subextensions L of K^sep/K, intertwining ρ with the maps σ_L^♮ : H^i(X_L) → H^i(X_{σL}); G_L fixes the image of H^i(X_L, M_L); hence every element has open stabiliser and H^i(X_C, M_C) is a discrete G_K-module.

api.name: fixed
api.statement: G_L acts trivially on the image of H^i(X_L)

api.name: discrete
api.statement: H^i(X_C,M_C) = ⋃_L H^i(X_C,M_C)^{G_L}, a discrete G_K-module

tests.name: point
tests.statement: X = Spa(K,𝒪_K): the colimit is the stalk ℱ_{ξ_C}

tests.name: not_qc
tests.statement: K = ℚ_p, ℓ ≠ p, X = ⊔_m Spa(K) with μ_{ℓ^m} on the m-th component: the compatible system of roots in ∏_m μ_{ℓ^m}(C) has non-open stabiliser ker χ_ℓ

tests.name: structure_sheaf
tests.statement: for 𝒪_{X_ét} as abelian sheaf on Spa(K) the colimit is K^sep, not C

tests.name: separable_index
tests.statement: for K = 𝔽_p((t)) only separable L are needed since C is the completion of K^sep

targets.name: schemeGaloisAction_colimit
targets.statement: For X a qcqs k-scheme and M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), colim_L H^i(X_L, M) ≅ H^i(X_{k^sep}, M) over finite subextensions L of k^sep/k, compatibly with ρ; G_L fixes the image of H^i(X_L, M); H^i(X_{k^sep}, M) is a discrete G_k-module.

tests.name: point
tests.statement: X = Spec k: H⁰ = ℱ_{k^sep}, higher groups vanish

tests.name: not_qc
tests.statement: X = ⊔_m Spec ℚ with μ_{ℓ^m} on the m-th component: non-open stabiliser ker χ_ℓ

targets.name: higherDirectImage_galoisModule
targets.statement: For f : X → Spa(K,𝒪_K) a qcqs rigid K-space and M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ): under the equivalence of sheaves of Λ-modules on Spa(K,𝒪_K)_ét with discrete Λ[G_K]-modules (stalk at ξ_C, action of 0.3), R^i f_* M corresponds to (H^i(X_C, M_C), ρ), naturally in M and compatibly with connecting maps. Consequently Hom(R^i f_*ℱ, R^j f_*𝒢) ≅ Hom_{Λ[G_K]}(H^i(X_C,ℱ_C), H^j(X_C,𝒢_C)); morphisms R^i f_*ℱ → Λ give G_K-invariant linear forms; base change along g : X′ → X corresponds to g_C^*.

api.name: hom_bijection
api.statement: sheaf morphisms between higher direct images = ρ-equivariant maps

api.name: invariant_forms
api.statement: maps to Λ give invariant linear forms

api.name: base_change
api.statement: base change corresponds to g_C^*

tests.name: induced
tests.statement: X = Spa(L,𝒪_L): f_*ℤ ↔ the permutation module ℤ[G_K/G_L], induced from the trivial representation of G_L; regular only for L/K Galois

tests.name: trace
tests.statement: the trace t_X of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §9.7 satisfies t_X∘ρ(σ) = t_X; for ℙ¹_K, t_X(c₁(𝒪(1))) = 1 with c₁ invariant

tests.name: convention
tests.statement: X = Spa(K), μ_n: both sides μ_n(C) with ζ ↦ σ(ζ); the stalk rule v̄ ↦ v̄∘Spa(σ̂⁻¹) is a right action

targets.name: schemeHigherDirectImage_galoisModule
targets.statement: For f : X → Spec k qcqs and M ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), under SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.15's equivalence (stalk at Spec k^sep, action of Stacks 03QW), R^i f_* M corresponds to (H^i(X_{k^sep}, M), ρ), with the consequences of 2.3.

tests.name: induced
tests.statement: X = Spec k′, k′/k finite separable: f_*ℤ ↔ ℤ[G_k/G_{k′}]

tests.name: real
tests.statement: k = ℝ, X = Spec ℂ: f_*μ_4 ↔ μ_4(ℂ)², conjugation = swap composed with ζ ↦ ζ̄

targets.name: hochschildSerre_galois
targets.statement: For X qcqs (rigid over K, resp. scheme over k) and ℱ a sheaf of Λ-modules, the Leray spectral sequence of X → Spa(K,𝒪_K) (resp. Spec k) becomes E_2^{p,q} = H^p_cont(G_K, (H^q(X_C, ℱ_C), ρ)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, ℱ), natural in ℱ, with edge map pr_C^* : H^n(X,ℱ) → H^n(X_C,ℱ_C)^{G_K}; for rigid X it agrees from E_2 on with ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §1.3(b) for the pro-finite-étale G_K-torsor X_{K^sep} → X, whose G_K-module structure on H^q(X_{K^sep}, ν^*ℱ) ≅ H^q(X_C, ℱ_C) is ρ.

tests.name: point
tests.statement: X = Spa(K): collapses to H^p_cont(G_K, ℱ_{ξ_C})

tests.name: shapiro
tests.statement: X = Spa(L): E_2 concentrated in q = 0, Shapiro gives H^p(G_L, ℱ_{ξ_C})

tests.name: direction
tests.statement: K = ℚ_2, μ_5: H²(Spa ℚ_2, μ_5) ≅ Br(ℚ_2)[5] ≅ ℤ/5 = H²(G, μ_5) with ζ ↦ σ(ζ); with ζ ↦ σ⁻¹(ζ) (= ℤ/5(−1)) local duality gives 0 since 2² ≢ 1 mod 5

targets.name: schemeGaloisAction_eq_adicFunctoriality
targets.statement: For X locally Noetherian over k, ℓ invertible in k and coefficient descent data (M_n) in EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.1's category, the finite level H^i(X_{k^sep}, M_n) of §F.4.6's continuous G_k-action is ρ, compatibly with reductions. For k = 𝔽_q, ρ(φ) of the arithmetic Frobenius is the inverse of §F.10.2's geometric Frobenius on H^i(X_{k̄}, M_n), using F_{X/k} × id = F_{X_{k̄}} ∘ φ_X⁻¹.

tests.name: mu
tests.statement: X = Spec 𝔽_q, μ_{ℓ^n}: ρ(φ) = ×q, geometric Frobenius ×q⁻¹, composite id

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: finite constant sheaf of a geometric point: both actions trivial

tests.name: P1
tests.statement: H²(ℙ¹_{k̄}, ℤ/ℓ^n) = ℤ/ℓ^n(−1): ρ(φ) = q⁻¹, geometric Frobenius q, matching §F.10.2b's geometric trace q

targets.name: adicCohomology
targets.statement: For a rigid K-space X, a prime ℓ and j ∈ ℤ (j = 0 if ℓ = char K), with T_j = (ℤ/ℓ^n(j))_n: the naive group H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) := lim_n H^i(X_C, ℤ/ℓ^n(j)) with the inverse-limit topology of discrete groups and action lim_n ρ; the continuous group H^i_cont(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) := H^i(X_C, Rlim_n (T_j)_C) = H^i(Rlim_n RΓ(X_C, ℤ/ℓ^n(j))) with action (σ_X)^♮ via σ_X^{-1}Rlim ≅ Rlim σ_X^{-1} and levelwise c_σ.
hypotheses: ℓ invertible in K when j ≠ 0

api.name: left_action
api.statement: both actions are left actions by ℤ_ℓ-linear automorphisms

api.name: milnor
api.statement: equivariant exact 0 → lim¹ H^{i−1}(ℤ/ℓ^n(j)) → H^i_cont → H^i → 0; equality under Mittag–Leffler

api.name: reduction
api.statement: RΓ_cont ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ^m ≅ RΓ(X_C, ℤ/ℓ^m(j)) equivariantly; Bockstein sequences

api.name: proetale
api.statement: for K ⊇ ℚ_p, ℓ = p: H^i_cont ≅ H^i(X_{C,proét}, Ẑ_p(j)) equivariantly

api.name: restriction
api.statement: for finite L ⊆ K̄, groups of X_L = groups of X with restricted action

tests.name: point_twist
tests.statement: X = Spa(K), j = 1: H⁰ = lim μ_{ℓ^n}(C) = ℤ_ℓ(1) along ℓ-th power maps, action by χ_ℓ

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: X = ∅: all groups vanish

tests.name: product
tests.statement: X = ⊔_m Spa(K): naive H⁰(X_C, ℤ_ℓ) = ∏_m ℤ_ℓ with the ℓ-adic (inverse-limit) topology, open subgroups ℓ^n ∏_m ℤ_ℓ, strictly finer than the product topology and not compact (∏_m ℤ/ℓ is an infinite discrete quotient); not finitely generated

tests.name: lim1
tests.statement: the tower (ℤ, ×ℓ) has lim¹ = ℤ_ℓ/ℤ ≠ 0: naive and continuous groups are distinct constructions

tests.name: charp
tests.statement: ℓ = char K = p, X closed disc: H¹(X_C, ℤ/p) = C⟨T⟩/{g^p − g} infinite; no ℤ/p(1)

targets.name: adicCohomology_continuous
targets.statement: For X qcqs, the action G_K × H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) → H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) is jointly continuous; H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) is an object of Mathlib's TopRep ℤ_ℓ G_K; ρ with this joint continuity is a TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_ℓ H on the whole group H = H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)), torsion included, whose TauCeti.ContinuousRep.toContRepresentation is the ContRepresentation of the TopRep object; when H is finite free with the ℓ-adic topology it lies in the finite projective subcategory of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.0 and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §1.1; the maps of 1.3 are continuous and equivariant in the limit.

tests.name: cyclotomic
tests.statement: X = Spa(K), j = 1: the action is TauCeti.continuousLocalCyclotomicCharacter ℓ K

tests.name: joint
tests.statement: ℤ_ℓ^× acting on discrete ℚ_ℓ: continuous operators, not jointly continuous

tests.name: not_qc
tests.statement: X = ⊔_m Spa(K(μ_{ℓ^m})), K = ℚ_p, ℓ ≠ p: an element of H⁰(X_C, ℤ/ℓ) has stabiliser G_{K(μ_{ℓ^∞})}, not open

tests.name: torsion_carrier
tests.statement: ℤ_ℓ/ℓ, discrete, trivial G_K-action: the action map (σ, x) ↦ x is continuous, so it is a TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_ℓ (ℤ_ℓ/ℓ) although ℓ·1 = 0 and it is not projective over ℤ_ℓ

targets.name: rationalCohomology
targets.statement: For a topological ℤ_ℓ-module A with a jointly continuous ℤ_ℓ-linear G_K-action, i.e. a TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_ℓ A (A = H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) of 3.2 with its inverse-limit topology), V := A ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} ℚ_ℓ = A[1/ℓ] with j_A : A → V carries the topology whose basic neighbourhoods of zero are the ℤ_ℓ-submodules Ω ⊆ V with ⋃_n ℓ^{−n}Ω = V and j_A^{-1}(ℓ^r Ω) open in A for all r ≥ 0 (the finest non-archimedean locally convex topology making j_A continuous); H^i(X_C, ℚ_ℓ(j)) := H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} ℚ_ℓ with this topology and action ρ ⊗ id. V is a topological ℚ_ℓ-vector space with the universal property for continuous ℤ_ℓ-linear maps from A to such spaces, the G_K-action is jointly continuous (an object of TopRep ℚ_ℓ G_K and a TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℚ_ℓ V, for every such A), and the construction is functorial. j_A(A) need not be open and V need not be Hausdorff; if A is finitely generated with its ℓ-adic topology (automatic for finitely generated H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j))), j_A(A) is an open lattice, V is finite-dimensional with its Hausdorff vector-space topology and lies in the finite projective subcategory of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.0.
hypotheses: A a topological ℤ_ℓ-module with jointly continuous ℤ_ℓ-linear G_K-action
for H^i(X_C, ℚ_ℓ(j)): X quasi-compact and quasi-separated
finite generation (with the ℓ-adic topology) for the finite-dimensional clause

locator.where: proof of Theorem 3.3.2, page 39, line 1706 (algebraic localisation H^i(ℚ_ℓ) = H^i(ℤ_ℓ)[1/ℓ] only)

api.name: universal
api.statement: V is a topological ℚ_ℓ-vector space, j_A is continuous, and continuous ℤ_ℓ-linear maps from A to non-archimedean locally convex ℚ_ℓ-spaces extend uniquely and continuously to V

api.name: joint_continuity
api.statement: the G_K-action on V is jointly continuous, via G_K-stable basic neighbourhoods ⋂_σ σ(Ω) (compactness of G_K and joint continuity on A)

api.name: functorial
api.statement: functorial for the continuous equivariant maps of 3.2

api.name: fg
api.statement: for A finitely generated with its ℓ-adic topology, j_A(A) is an open lattice and V is finite-dimensional, in the finite projective subcategory of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.0; for H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) finite generation forces the ℓ-adic topology

tests.name: torsion
tests.statement: A = ℤ_ℓ/ℓ gives V = 0

tests.name: twist
tests.statement: A = ℤ_ℓ(1) gives ℚ_ℓ(1) with its ℓ-adic topology (basic neighbourhoods ℓ^kℤ_ℓ(1)), character χ_ℓ, j_A(A) open

tests.name: product_topology
tests.statement: A = ∏_m ℤ_ℓ with the product topology and trivial action (the limit of (ℤ/ℓ^n)^n under truncation and reduction): ℓA is not open, so no vector-space topology makes j_A(A) open with its own topology; here the lattices {v : v_1..v_M ∈ ℓ^kℤ_ℓ} are basic, V is Hausdorff and j_A(A) is not open

tests.name: product
tests.statement: (∏_ℕ ℤ_ℓ) ⊗ ℚ_ℓ (common denominators) is a proper subspace of ∏_ℕ ℚ_ℓ, not containing (ℓ^{−m})_m

tests.name: discrete
tests.statement: for A = ℤ_ℓ the topology on ℚ_ℓ is ℓ-adic; with the discrete topology, scalar multiplication ℤ_ℓ × ℚ_ℓ → ℚ_ℓ is not continuous at (0, 1)

tests.name: indiscrete
tests.statement: A = ℚ_ℓ indiscrete: the only basic neighbourhood is V, so V is indiscrete; Hausdorffness is not automatic

targets.name: galoisAction_twist
targets.statement: For n invertible in K, Λ a ℤ/n-algebra, ℱ a sheaf of Λ-modules and j ∈ ℤ: (μ_n(C))_{X_C} ≅ (μ_n)_C canonically, intertwining c_σ with σ on μ_n(C); H^i(X_C, ℱ(j)_C) ≅ H^i(X_C, ℱ_C) ⊗_{ℤ/n} μ_n(C)^{⊗j} (Λ acting through the first factor; = H^i(X_C, ℱ_C) ⊗_Λ Λ(j)(C) for commutative Λ) is G_K-equivariant; for ℓ invertible in K the ℤ_ℓ, continuous and ℚ_ℓ versions hold with the Tate twist of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §1.2; the same on schemes; an arithmetic Frobenius lift acts on ℤ_ℓ(1) by q.

tests.name: coordinate
tests.statement: replacing ζ by ζ^u multiplies the coordinate of a fixed element of 𝔽_p(1) by u⁻¹; the canonical isomorphism needs no choice

tests.name: P1
tests.statement: H²(ℙ¹_C, ℤ/n(1)) = ℤ/n trivial, H²(ℙ¹_C, ℤ/n) = ℤ/n(−1)

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: j = 0 gives the identity; n = 1 all groups vanish

tests.name: elliptic
tests.statement: H¹(E_C, ℤ/n) has determinant χ_n⁻¹; the wrong twist gives χ_n³, differing at Frobenius for n = 7, K = ℚ_2 (4 vs 1 mod 7)

targets.name: properComparison_equivariant
targets.statement: For a proper K-scheme Y, Λ torsion and M ∈ D⁺(Y_ét, Λ), Huber's comparison for Spa(C,𝒪_C) → Spec K gives H^i(Y_{K^sep}, M) ≅ (R^i f_*M)_{Spec C} ≅ H^i((Y^an)_C, M^an); it is G_K-equivariant (scheme action on the left, ρ on the right) by naturality in Spa(C,𝒪_C) over Spec K, and factors through the equivariant isomorphisms H^i(Y_{K̄}, M) ≅ H^i(Y_C, M) (proper base change) and H^i(Y_C, M) ≅ H^i((Y^an)_C, M^an).

locator.where: Theorem 7.1.1, page 128, line 4584 (compactly supported comparison for compactifiable schemes and all torsion sheaves); with huber1996 Theorem 3.7.2, page 226, through ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §8.2

tests.name: finite
tests.statement: Y = Spec L: Λ^{Hom_K(L,K̄)} with the permutation action on embeddings (induced from the trivial representation of G_L) on all sides

tests.name: curve
tests.statement: smooth proper curve: H¹(−, μ_n) = J[n] on each side via Kummer and GAGA

tests.name: P1
tests.statement: Y = ℙ¹: H² = ℤ/n(−1), arithmetic Frobenius acts by q⁻¹; p-torsion allowed

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: Y = ∅: all groups vanish

targets.name: finiteness_toContinuousRep
targets.statement: For X qcqs rigid, ℓ prime, j ∈ ℤ (j = 0 if ℓ = char K), i ≥ 0: (a) H^i(X_C, ℤ/ℓ) finite ⇒ all H^i(X_C, ℤ/ℓ^n(j)) finite; (b) H^{i−1}, H^i(X_C, ℤ/ℓ) finite ⇒ H^i_cont = H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)), finitely generated (topological Nakayama Module.Finite.of_quotient_smul_top with R = ℤ_ℓ, I = (ℓ), H compact Hausdorff, H/ℓH ⊆ H^i(X_C, ℤ/ℓ(j)) finite), inverse-limit topology = ℓ-adic; (c) under (b), H = H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) with its ℓ-adic topology is a finitely generated TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_ℓ H (3.2), torsion included; H_tors is finite and G_K-stable, H/H_tors is finite free and, with the quotient (ℓ-adic) topology, a TauCeti.ContinuousRep in the finite projective subcategory of EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.4.0; H^i(X_C, ℚ_ℓ(j)) is a finite-dimensional TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℚ_ℓ; (d) vanishing of H^q(X_C, ℤ/ℓ) for all q > N gives vanishing of the ℤ/ℓ^n(j), ℤ_ℓ(j), H_cont ℤ_ℓ(j) and ℚ_ℓ(j) groups for all q > N, with no finiteness hypothesis: 0 → ℤ/ℓ(j) → ℤ/ℓ^{n+1}(j) → ℤ/ℓ^n(j) → 0 and H^{N+1}(X_C, ℤ/ℓ(j)) = 0 make the transitions of (H^N(X_C, ℤ/ℓ^n(j)))_n surjective, so lim¹ = 0 (TauCeti.ModuleTower.isMittagLeffler_of_surjective, subsingleton_limOne_of_isMittagLeffler) and the Milnor sequence gives H^{N+1}_cont = 0.

locator.where: Theorem 19.2, page 125, line 4860 (finite generation for flat ℤ_ℓ-sheaves on varieties over a separably closed field; the route here is dévissage, §3.1 and topological Nakayama)

tests.name: point
tests.statement: X = Spa(K): H⁰ = ℤ_ℓ(j), higher groups vanish

tests.name: torsion
tests.statement: Enriques surface analytified, char K = 0, ℓ = 2: H = H²(X_C, ℤ_2) ≅ ℤ_2^{10} ⊕ ℤ/2 is a TauCeti.ContinuousRep G_K ℤ_2 H with nonzero torsion, outside the finite projective subcategory; H/H_tors ≅ ℤ_2^{10} lies in it; the torsion dies in H²(X_C, ℚ_2), of dimension 10

tests.name: top_degree_surjective
tests.statement: K = 𝔽_2((t)), ℓ = 2, j = 0, X the closed unit disc: H^q(X_C, 𝔽_2) = 0 for q ≥ 2 (Artin–Schreier, affinoid acyclicity), so N = 1, while H¹(X_C, 𝔽_2) = C⟨T⟩/{g² − g} is infinite (T, T³, T⁵, … independent); the transitions H¹(ℤ/2^{n+1}) → H¹(ℤ/2^n) are surjective and H²_cont(X_C, ℤ_2) = 0. For X = Spa(K), N = 0, H¹_cont = 0. The ×ℓ tower of 3.1 (lim¹ = ℤ_ℓ/ℤ) has non-surjective transitions and is not a degree-N tower under (d)

tests.name: open_disc
tests.statement: open unit disc, ℓ = p residue characteristic: hypothesis of (a) fails, H¹(X_C, ℤ_p) not finitely generated

targets.name: finiteness_instances
targets.statement: For a rigid K-space X of dimension d, the hypotheses of 4.3 with N = 2d hold when (a) X smooth proper and ℓ invertible in 𝒪_K; (b) X smooth proper, char K = 0, ℓ = p the residue characteristic; (c) X = Y^an for a proper K-scheme Y and ℓ invertible in K; (d) X proper and ℓ invertible in 𝒪_K (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §11.1 when X_C is locally algebraically of finite type over Spa(C,𝒪_C); the gap proper-rigid-finiteness for the remaining proper X). Hence the finite levels are finite, H^i(X_C, ℤ_ℓ(j)) is finitely generated, H^i(X_C, ℚ_ℓ(j)) is a finite-dimensional continuous G_K-representation, all vanishing for i > 2d.

locator.where: Theorem 5.1, page 28, line 1279 (case (b)); berkovich1993 Corollary 7.4.4, page 143 (case (a))

tests.name: projective
tests.statement: ℙ^d: H^{2m} = ℤ_ℓ(−m) for 0 ≤ m ≤ d, odd groups 0

tests.name: charp
tests.statement: ℓ = char K: no case applies; no finiteness claimed

tests.name: unipotence
tests.statement: quasi-unipotence of inertia (Hansen–Zavyalov 3.3.1–3.3.2) is not claimed

tests.name: disc
tests.statement: closed disc, ℓ = p, char K = 0: H¹ infinite; properness is used

gaps.title: Finiteness of prime-to-residue cohomology of proper rigid spaces
gaps.detail: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology §9.7 proves finiteness of H^i(X, L) for proper smooth rigid X over an algebraically closed complete rank-one C and n invertible in 𝒪_C (Berkovich 7.4.4). §11.1 proves finiteness for qcqs X locally algebraically of finite type over C (Huber, Proposition 6.1.1), with constructible coefficients killed by n prime to the residue characteristic. Case (d) of 4.4 needs the same for proper X that need not be smooth; the gap is the proper spaces without a locally algebraically finite-type presentation. The statement is Huber, A finiteness result for the compactly supported cohomology of rigid analytic varieties II, Ann. Inst. Fourier 57 (2007), Corollary 5.6 (with Corollary 5.4 for compact supports), with no hypothesis on the characteristic of C.
gaps.needs: Finiteness of H^i(X, ℤ/n) for every proper rigid space X over an algebraically closed complete rank-one field C and every n invertible in 𝒪_C, without smoothness.
